To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(31)P nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy and first principles DFT calculations are powerful techniques for the study of Ti/Ge distribution and disorder in NASICON-type compounds.
(31)P chemical shift calculations of LiTi2-x Gex(PO4)(3) NASICON series by using DFT method are in good agreement with the experimental (31)P spectra.
the Ti/Ge disorder in LiTi2−xGex(PO 4) 3 NASICON series is detected by 31P MAS NMR, and that the disorder is random in next nearest neighbor sites that surround tetraedrical PO4 units.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of (31)P solid-state NMR spectroscopy to analyze the Ti/Ge disorder in LiTi2Ge(PO4) 3 and LiTi1.5Ge1.5(PO4)2 NASICON series.
a detailed study of the local environment around P atoms in NASICON series by means of (31)P solid-state MAS NMR spectroscopy and DFT calculations.
a complete description of the Ti/Ge distribution and its effect on (31) P MAS NMR signals in the LiTi2- xGex(PO3)3 series.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the random distribution of Ti and Ge is not only limited to the NNN sites but it is extended up to 3rd NN sites.
, in the LiTi2- xGex(PO)4 series, the Ti/Ge substitution is random, both in NNN sites and in the R3̅ c symmetry.
, in the LiTi2- xGex(PO)4 series, Ti/Ge disorder in NNN sites of the R3̅ symmetry is random.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the Ti/Ge distribution at NNN sites of the R3̅ c NASICON series is random, and this distribution is not affected by the Ti/Ge ratio in the sample, but it depends only on the overall symmetry of the crystal.

(31)P nuclear magnetic resonance is a powerful tool to follow Ti/ Ge disorder, and that first-principles calculations are essential to assign the different components detected in (31) P MAS NMR spectra. (31)P and Ti/Ge disorder have been also analyzed by Rietveld refinement.
(31)P chemical shieldings of the NASICON series are mainly influenced by Ti/Ge distribution, but also by the charge of the O atoms that are bonded to the tetrahedral PO(4) units.
The main takeaway from our work is that
(31)P and first-principels DFT calculations can be used to study the local structure and Ti/Ge distribution on NNN positions in NASICON-type compounds.
NMR is an excellent tool to follow Ti/ Ge disorder, and that the combination of NMR and DFT calculations allows us to determine the Ti/Ge distribution on a local scale.
(31)P solid-state NMR is an ideal tool to analyze the distribution of Ti and Ge in NASICON-type compounds, which is of interest for their use as cathode materials in Li-ion batteries.
